Thanks for the kind words, Rana_Hamza.

I’m not sure if I understand your question correctly, but I’ll try to answer it to the best of my knowledge:

My mod does not need to be installed on the Fika headless client. In fact, I would recommend NOT installing it on the headless client and adding it to the Exclusions.json file of Corter’s ModSync, if you are using this plugin.

If no price information is displayed in-raid, then something is wrong. Check the “SPT/BepInEx/LogOutput.log” log file. There you should find something like “:

SwiftXP.ShowMeTheMoney] Ragfair price table was queried!”.

If you can’t find this line, the mod is maybe not installed correctly. If you can see both Trader and Flea Market prices in the character/stash screen, the mod should be working correctly – even in-raid. If the problem persists, you can send me your logs in the Mod Support Forum and I’ll take a look to see if something is wrong when I have time. Please follow this link to the SPT FAQ to find your logs. You can also use the SPT.Launcher => Settings > Copy logs to clipboard.

I have also updated my mod description based on your comment. Thank you.

comments.author: swiftxp
comments.body_html:
Yes, the base price of the weapon will continue to be shown as in older versions, followed by the total price for all mods (in the new line) without the base price of the weapon.

I also tested adding the price of the mods to the base price of the weapon and also tested adding up only the price of all mods without the base price of the weapon for the flea-price (as LootValue does, for example), but this gives the false impression that you can sell the weapon for this price on the Flea Market, which was not the case in many of my tests as the price was much higher due to the mods. For example, I took two base AK-74N. One I sold for the base price (~40k). The other one I modded a little bit and tried to sell it for the price of installed mods (~280k). The modded AK-74N was not purchased for this price. I did more tests with the same result and that’s why I’ve now decided to go this route. Of course, it may be that I made a mistake during testing; I don’t want to rule that out. Ultimately, I just want to make sure that the price shown is the price at which the item will actually sell for in the end. For the new line I thought to myself: Hey, you basically want to know if expensive mods are installed on the weapon. What’s the easiest way to tell?

comments.author: swiftxp
comments.body_html:
Hi! I finally had a chance to look into this. The flea market simulation in SPT still has some gaps in certain areas. For example, an “NVG strap” on its own is worth ~112k on the flea market. However, if I attach an “N-15” night vision device (flea market value ~176k) to that strap, you cannot sell the combined unit for the total price of both parts on the flea market.

In other words, if I try to sell the NVG strap with the N-15 attached for ~228k, SPT only sees the base item (the strap) and will set the sale probability for that high price to nearly 0%. Consequently, the NVG strap with night vision for ~228k simply won’t sell. I also did some tests with some helmets and attachments.

My mod mirrors this behavior and only displays the price at which the item is guaranteed (100% chance) to sell. I can’t rule out that my mod might not perfectly replicate SPT’s logic in every single case, but I always strive to reflect the current SPT integration. For weapons, for instance, SPT is now capable of factoring attachments into the flea market price, and my mod reflects that as well.

I’m considering adding a note to the tooltip to indicate whether the displayed flea market price refers only to the base item or to the item combination.

Thanks again for your feedback!
